Builds calibrated isoscapes, i.e. isoscapes of samples (e.g. tissues)

Source: R/calibscape.R
calibscape.Rd

This function uses a calibration fit to convert the mean isoscape of source isotopic values (e.g. precipitation) into a calibrated isoscape, i.e. the mean isoscape of the isotopic values expected in the samples (e.g. animal tissues).

Usage

calibscape(isoscape, calibfit)

Arguments

isoscape

The output of the function isoscape or isomultiscape (i.e. an object of class ISOSCAPE)

calibfit

The output of the function calibfit (i.e. an object of class CALIBFIT)

Value

This function returns a list of class ISOSCAPE and CALIBSCAPE containing a SpatRaster with a single layer (mean) storing the predicted mean isotopic values of the samples, and the location of the sources and of the calibration samples (except for the calibration method "desk") as spatial points.

Details

For assignments, IsoriX converts the isotopic values of the samples to assign (e.g. animal tissues) into isotopic values of the sources (e.g. precipitation), and not the other way around (see isofind). Yet, it can be useful to visualise or study what the isoscape would look like in terms of sample values. This is what calibscape() does.

The calibration fit (see calibfit) models the relationship sample_value = intercept + slope * source_value, whatever the calibration method used (for the method "desk_inverse", the inversion of the regression is already performed by calibfit). The mean isoscape is thus simply calibrated by computing, in each raster cell, intercept + slope * mean, using the estimates of the intercept and of the slope stored in the calibration fit.

Only the mean isoscape is converted. The variances (prediction, residual and response variances) are not converted since their conversion would require to account for the uncertainty of the calibration fit, which depends on the calibration method being used. The isoscapes related to the residual dispersion are not returned either.

The output can be plotted using plot.ISOSCAPE (with which = "mean" only; by default, the plot shows the location of the calibration samples instead of that of the sources), but it cannot be used for assignments (isofind) or to simulate data (create_aliens), since these functions require isoscapes of source isotopic values.

See also

isoscape and isomultiscape for the functions building the isoscapes of sources

calibfit for the function fitting the calibration

plot.ISOSCAPE for the function plotting isoscapes

Examples


## The examples below will only be run if sufficient time is allowed
## You can change that by typing e.g. options_IsoriX(example_maxtime = XX)
## if you want to allow for examples taking up to ca. XX seconds to run
## (so don't write XX but put a number instead!)

if (getOption_IsoriX("example_maxtime") > 30) {
  ## We fit the models
  GNIPDataDEagg <- prepsources(data = GNIPDataDE)
  GermanFit <- isofit(
    data = GNIPDataDEagg,
    mean_model_fix = list(elev = TRUE, lat_abs = TRUE)
  )

  ## We build the isoscapes of sources (precipitation)
  GermanScape <- isoscape(raster = ElevRasterDE, isofit = GermanFit)

  ## We define a calibration fit from published estimates
  CalibDataDesk <- data.frame(intercept = -10, slope = 0.8)
  CalibDesk <- calibfit(data = CalibDataDesk, method = "desk")

  ## We build the calibrated isoscape (i.e. the isoscape of tissues)
  GermanCalibScape <- calibscape(isoscape = GermanScape, calibfit = CalibDesk)

  GermanCalibScape
  plot(GermanCalibScape)
}
